senses.text: alphabetical letter The sixth letter of the alphabet: called HaA='N [and HaA (respecting which latter see the letter b ). It is one of the letters termed mahomuwsap , or nonvocal, i. e. pronounced with the breath only, without the voice; and of those termed Haloqiy~ap i. e. faucial, or guttural, for] the place of its utterance is in the fauces; and were it not for a hoarse aspiration with which it is pronounced, it would resemble E : next after it [with respect to the place of utterance] is h : [ E having the lowest place of utterance; then H ; and then h :] and H and h are never consociated in any uncompounded word of the which the letters are all radicals, because of the mutual nearness of their places of utterance: they occur together in Hay~ahalo ; but this is only a compound word in t

is a particle, used in three senses: (Mughnee:) it is a particle denoting the end of an extent; (Mughnee, K;) which is its predominant meaning; (Mughnee;) asserted by some to be always its meaning: (TA:) and denoting a cause, or motive: and syn. with A_il~aA as an exceptive; (Mughnee, K;) which last is the rarest, and is mentioned by few. 82 of the Arabic text;) others reading yaquwla , which, as well as yaquwlu , here means qaAla . (Jel.) ― -b7- [Respecting the cases in which the mansoob aor. is used after HA~Y , and those in which the marfooa aor. is used, the following observations are made.] When Ht~Y precedes a future, the latter is mansoob, by reason of A^ano understood before it, as in the saying, sirotu A_ilY Alkuwfapi Hat~aY A^adoxulahaA [ I journeyed to El-Koofeh until I entered it: see above]: (S:) it is not mansoob unless the verb is a future: if it is future with respect to the time of speaking, it must be mansoob, as in Hat~aY yarojiEa A_ilayonaA muwsaY [cited above]: if the verb is future with respect to what precedes, only, it may be mansoob, as in Hat~aY yaquwla Alr~asuwlu [mentioned above]

senses.text: 1 , aor. , is a verb mentioned by IKoot and IKtt and others, as derived from HatofN signifying “ death, ” though J says that no verb is formed from this word; as IF and Meyd and Az also assert: (MF, TA:) and HutuwfN is its inf. n., as well as pl. of HatofN : [accord. to SM, it is intrans., signifying He died; for he says,] hence the saying in the A, Almaro'u yasoEaY wayaTuwfu waEaAqibatuhu AlHutuwfu [ Man labours, and goes about: and his end is dying ]. [But see what follows.] -A2- IF says that no verb is formed from HatofN signifying “ death; ” and so, after him, J; and Az says that he had heard no such verb: but IKoot mentions Hatafahu , aor. , inf. n. Death: (S, Msb, K, &c.:) pl. HutuwfN . (S, K.) You say, maAta Hatofa A^anofihi , (A 'Obeyd, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and Hatofa fiyhi , but this is rare, and Hatofa A^anofayohi , (K,) which may mean manoxirayohi , or it may mean A^anofh wafamh , the Anf being made predominant, (TA,) He died upon his bed; (A 'Obeyd, Mgh, Msb, K;) [ a natural death; ] respiring until he yielded his last breath; (Msb;) not from slaughter, nor beating, (A 'Obeyd, S, Msb, K,) nor drowning, nor burning, (A 'Obeyd, Sgh, Msb, K,) nor by a wild beast, &c.: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) the nose is particularized as meaning that the spirit passes forth from it with the breath

; or because they imagined that the spirit of the sick man passes forth from his nose, and that of the wounded man from his wound; (IAth, K;) or because the spirit passes forth from the mouth and the nose, and the latter of these is made predominant: (O, TA:) and Htf is put in the accus. case in the manner of an inf. n. (TA.) This phrase was used in the time of paganism, by Es-Semow-al: (Msb, TA:) or, accord. to some, in the phrase attributed to him, the right reading is not mAt Htf Anfh , but mAt fiY firaA$ihi ; and the former was first used by Mohammad. (Ham p.

52.) It is said of a human being: (S, Mgh:) and then of any animal when it dies without any accidental cause: (Mgh:) hence, of a fish that has died, and floats upon the water. (Msb, TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Ámir Ibn-Fuheyreh, waAlmaro'u yaA^otiY Hatofuhu mino fawoqihi [ And man, his death comes from above him ]: meaning that his caution and his cowardice will not repel from him the decree of death when it befalls him: originally said by 'Amr Ibn-Mámeh. (L, TA.) -A2- Hay~apN HatofapN [ A dead serpent ] is a phrase like AimoraA^apN EadolapN : (Z, TA:) the latter word is here an epithet. (Z, K.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. Haj~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He repaired, or betook himself, to, or towards, syn. qaSada , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) a person (S, A, Mgh) [or place], in an absolute sense: or to, or towards, an object of reverence, veneration, respect, or honour: or, accord. to Kh, he repaired, or betook himself, much, or frequently, to, or towards, an object of this kind: and also he repaired to, betook himself to, or visited, a person: (TA:) and he went to, or visited, a person repeatedly, or frequently. (ISk, T, S, Mgh, K. *) You say also, Haj~a banuw fulaAnK fulaAnFA The sons of such a one continued long going repeatedly to visit such a one. (S.) ― -b2-

Hence, (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S,) and inf. n. Hij~N also, (Sb, L,) or this is a simple subst., (S, Msb, K,) by a conventional usage, (S,) or predominantly, (Mgh,) or by restriction of its usage in the law, (Msb,) He repaired to Mekkeh, (S, K,) or to the Kaabeh, (Mgh, Msb,) to perform the religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) or for the purpose of the Eumorap [q. v.; but this latter meaning is very rare: the usual meaning is, he performed the pilgrimage to Mekkeh and Mount' Arafát, with all the rites and ceremonies prescribed to be observed at, and between, those two places ]: (Msb:) or he repaired to the House [ of God, at Mekkeh, ] and performed the actions prescribed for that occasion by the law of the Kur-án and the Sunneh. (L.) [See Haj
Also, (TA,) inf. n. Haj~N , (K,) He came, or arrived. (K, TA.) You say, Haj~a EalayonaA fulaAnN Such a one came to us. (TA.) -A2-
Also, [aor., accord. to rule, as above,] inf. n. Haj~N , He shaved [his head; as one does on completing the performance of the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage: see Haj~N , below]. (TA.) -A3-

Also, (IAar, A, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. Haj~N , (TA,) He probed a fracture of the head, (K,) or a wound, (A, TA,) with a miHojaAj , (A, K,) or miyl , (TA,) for the purpose of curing it: (TA:) or he probed a wound to know its depth: (IAar, TA:) or he examined a cleft in the head to know whether there were in it bone or blood: (ISh, TA:) or he dressed and cured a wound in the head reaching to the brain: or he poured boiled clarified butter upon a fracture of the head, in consequence of which the blood was mixed with the brain, until the blood appeared, which he took away with a little cotton: (TA:) or Haj~ahu , inf. n. Haj~N , signifies he probed a fracture of his head for the purpose of curing it: (S:) or he made a perforation in the bone [ of his broken head ] ( qadaHa fiyhi ) with an iron in

Prov. ” ii. 452]. (TA.) -A5-

(TA.) ― -b3-

Also, inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He made a writing &c. accurate, or exact; (S, K;) he made a writing beautiful, or elegant, and free from defects, by forming its characters rightly, and rectifying its faults : (A:) he wrote a writing well, or elegantly, and accurately, or exactly; (TK;) he wrote well, or elegantly : (KL:) and he made an account, or a reckoning, accurate, without mistake, and without omission, and without erasure. (TA.) [And simply (tropical:) He wrote a letter &c.]

1. ― -b2- Also His (a man's) camels became thirsty. (S, K.) -A2- Also He (God) made a man's liver to become dry by reason of thirst or grief. (TA.) May God make his bosom thirsty ]: or the meaning is haAmatahu [app. here used as signifying the bird called haAmap , in the form of which the soul was believed to issue from a slain man, and to call incessantly for drink until the slaughter of the slayer]. (TA.)

A_iHoraAmN . (S.) The saying Aall~`hu A^akobaru at the commencement of prayer is termed takobiyrapu Alt~aHoriymi [ The tkbyrp of prohibition ], because it prohibits the person praying from saying and doing anything extraneous to prayer: and it is also termed ↓ , meaning the tkbyrp of entering upon a state of prohibition by prayer. (TA.) It is said in a trad., of Ibn- 'Abbás, A_i*aA Har~ama Alr~ajulu A@moraA^atahu fahiYa yamiynN yukaf~iruhaA [ When the man declares his wife to be forbidden to him, it is an oath, which he must expiate ]: for the taHoriym of a wife and of a female slave may be
4 , [inf. n. A_iHoraAmN ,] He entered upon a thing [or state or time ] that caused what was before allowable, or lawful, to him to be forbidden, or unlawful. (S, * Msb. [See also

5.]) And hence, (S, Msb,) He purposed entering upon the performance of the Haj~ or the Eumorap : (Msb:) or he (the performer of the Haj~ or the Eumorap ) entered upon acts whereby what was allowable, or lawful, to him became forbidden, or unlawful; (K, TA;) as venereal intercourse, and the anointing of oneself, and wearing sewed garments, and hunting and the like: (TA:) you say, AHrAm biAlHaj~i and biAlEumorapi , because what was allowable to the person became forbidden; as the killing of objects of the chase, and [venereal intercourse with] women. (S.) And He entered into the Haram , i. e. Mekkeh or El-Medeeneh, (K, TA,) or the sacred territory of cither of those cities: (TA:) or he entered into a sacred, or an inviolable, state

; or into a state of security or safety, (S, K, TA,) being assured by a compact, or bond, that he should not be attacked [&c.]: (TA:) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (S,) he entered upon a sacred month; (S, Msb, K;) and so ↓ , (K, TA, [in the CK Harama ,]) inf. n. taHoriymN . (TA.) And He entered [as a subject] into the covenanted state of security of the government of the Khaleefeh. (TA.) 'Omar said, AlS~iyaAmu A_iHoraAmN [ Fasting is a state of prohibition ], because the faster is prohibited from doing that which would break his fast. (Sh, TA.) And Alr~ajulu yuHorimu fiY AlgaDabi , a saying of El-Hasan, means The man swears in anger, because he becomes prohibited thereby ( bihi ↓ ) [from doing, or refraining from, a thing]. (TA.) 8 He held him in reverence, respect, or honour; he reverenced, respected, or honoured, him. (MA.) [See HuromapN . Golius and Freytag explain AiHotarama as meaning “ Dignitate et præsidio venerabilis fuit: ” but it is the pass., AuHoturima , that has this meaning
; or rather, he was held in reverence, &c.; was reverenced, &c.]

It is said in a trad., of Adam, AisotaHorama baEoda mawoti A@bonihi miAy^apa sanapK lamo yaDoHako [ He deemed himself in a state of prohibition, after the death of his son, a hundred years, not laughing ]: from A^aHorama signifying “ he entered into a sacred, or an inviolable, state. ” (TA.) -A2- AstHrmt , said of a female cloven-hoofed animal, &c.: see

4 in the present art.]) Hence the saying, faEalahu fiY Hul~ihi waHuromihi , and ↓ , He did it when he was free from AHrAm and when he was in the state of AHrAm . (K in art. Hl .) And hence the saying of 'Áïsheh, respecting Mohammad, kunotu A^uTay~ibuhu liHul~ihi waHuromihi , i. e. [ I used to perfume him when he was free from AHrAm and ] when he was in the state of AHrAm : (S, Msb: *) or when he became free from AHrAm and when he performed the ablution and desired to enter upon the state of AHrAm for the Haj~ or the Eumorap . Showing much honour, (Mgh, K,) and manifesting joy or pleasure [ at meeting another ]; as also ↓ ; (K;) and behaving with affection, or benevolence and solicitude; (Mgh;) showing kindness, or goodness and affection and gentleness, and regard for the circumstances of another: (Lth, TA:) and asking, or inquiring, much respecting another's state, or condition; as also ↓ : (K:) going to the utmost length in asking, or inquiring: (S:) and [hence, perhaps,] knowing in the utmost degree: (S, K:) and importunate, pressing, or urgent, in asking, or inquiring: (K:) pl. HufawaA='u . (Fr, K.) You say, huwa HafiY~N bihi He is one who behaves with affection, or benevolence and solicitude, to him; who shows him much honour [&c.]. (Mgh.) A_in~ahu kaAna biY Hafiy~FA , in the Kur [xix. 48], means Verily He
: see HifowapN .

senses.text: 1 , aor. (S, Msb, K, &c.) and , (IDrd, Msb, K,) [the latter irregular,] inf. n. Haq~apN (K, TA) and Haq~N (IDrd, TA) and HuquwqN , (TA,) i. q. SaAra Haq~FA [i. e., accord. to the primary meaning of Haq~N , as explained below, on the authority of Er-Rághib, It was, or became, suitable to the requirements of wisdom, justice, right or rightness, truth, or reality or fact

; or to the exigencies of the case ]: (TA:) it was, or became, just, proper, right, correct, or true; authentic, genuine, sound, valid, substantial, or real; established, or confirmed, as a truth or fact: and necessitated, necessary, requisite, or unavoidable; binding, obligatory, incumbent, or due: syn. wajaba ; (T, S, Msb, K, &c.;) and vabata : (Msb, TA:) it was, or became, a manifest and an indubitable fact or event; as explained by IDrd in the Jm; (TA;) it happened, betided, or befell, surely, without doubt or uncertainty. (K.) It is said in the Kur xxxvi. 6, laqado Haq~a Alqawolu EalaY A^akovarihimo , i. e. The saying, “ I will assuredly fill Hell with genii and men together, ” [Kur xi.

120 and xxxii. 13,] (Bd,) or the sentence of punishment, (Jel,) hath become necessitated [ as suitable to the requirements of justice, or as being just or right, ] to take effect upon the greater number of them; syn. wajaba , (Jel, TA,) and vabata . (TA.) And this, namely, vabata , is the meaning of the verb in the phrase, Haq~a Ealayoka AlqaDaA='u [ The sentence was, or, emphatically, is, necessitated as suitable to the requirements of justice to take effect upon thee

; or it was, or is, necessary, just, or right, that the sentence should take effect upon thee ]. (TA.) [In like manner,] one says, yaHiq~u Ealayoka A^ano tafoEala ka*aA It is necessary for thee [ as suitable to the requirements of wisdom or justice or the like ], or incumbent on thee, or just or proper or right for thee, that thou shouldst do such a thing. (TA.) [Thus one says,] AlHaqiyqapu maA yaHiq~u Ealayoka A^ano taHomiyahu [ The Hqyqp is that which it is necessary for thee &c., or that which it behooveth thee, that thou shouldst defend it, or protect it ]. (S, * K.) Accord. to Sh, the Arabs said, Haq~a EalaY~a A^ano A^afoEala *`lika and Huq~a : but accord. to Fr, when you say Haq~a , you say Ealayoka ; and when you say Huq~a , you say laka . (TA.) [Accordingly] one says, Huq~a laka A^

2 and 5: (Bd, Jel: *) or Huqiqota biA^ano tafoEala may mean thou wast, or art, known by the testimony of thy circumstances to be Haqiyq &c. (A, TA.) And maA kaAna yaHuq~uka A^ano tafoEalahu [virtually] means the same as maA Huq~a laka [best rendered in this case It did not behoove thee to do it ]. (TA.) One says also, Haq~a A^ano tafoEala [ It was, or, emphatically, is, necessary &c. that thou shouldst do or to do such a thing]: but they did not say, Haqaqota A^ano tafoEala . (Fr, TA.) ― -b2- But Haq~a EalaY~a A^ano tafoEala ka*aA means Thy doing so distressed, or hath distressed, or afflicted, me

; or, emphatically, distresses, or afflicts, me; like Eaz~a EalaY~a . (S and K and TA in art. Ez .) And in like manner, Haq~a A^an~aka *aAhibN [or Haq~a maA A^an~aka *aAhibN ] means Eaz~a maA A^an~aka *aAhibN [ It is distressing to me that thou art going away ]. (TA in art. Ez .) And laHaq~a maA is used in the same manner as laEaz~a maA , q. v. (A and TA in art. Ez .) You say also, Haq~ati AlHaAjapu Want befell, or betided, or happened, and was severe, or distressing: (Msb, TA:) [which is said to be] from the phrase, Haq~ati AlqiyaAmapu , aor. , The resurrection included, or shall include, within its sphere [ all ] the created beings. (Msb.) -A2- Haq~ato , aor. , (K,) inf. n. Hiq~apN (S, * Msb, K,) and Hiq~N , (K,) or, accord. to ISd, it should rather be HaqaAqapN and HuquwqapN , because H
; or to the exigencies of the case; (see the first of the significations in this art.;) or] necessary, requisite, or unavoidable; binding, obligatory, incumbent, or due

; or just, proper, or right; syn. A^awojabahu ; (K;) [whence Huq~a laka A^ano tafoEala *aA , explained above;] as also ↓ (K) and ↓ ; (S, K;) which last some explain by Say~arahu Haq~FA [meaning as above

; or he rendered it true; ] or Sy~rh Hq~FA laA $ak~a fiyhi [ he rendered it true, so that there was no doubt respecting it ]; as also Haq~ahu , inf. n. Haq~N : and Haq~ahu signifies also he established it so that it became true and undoubted in his estimation: (TA:) or Haq~ahu signifies, (S, Msb,) or signifies also, (K,) he assured, or certified, himself of it; he ascertained it; he was, or became, sure, or certain, of it; (A 'Obeyd, S, Msb, * K; *) and so ↓ (A 'Obeyd, S, K) and ↓ : (S, Msb: *) or he pronounced it, or held or believed it, to be established as a necessary truth or fact; as also ↓ : and ↓ has a similar, but intensive, signification: (Msb:) or ↓ signifies he established it as true

; or he judged, or decided, it to be so: (TA: [ contr. of A^aboTalahu : see an ex., from the Kur viii., voce A^aboTala :]) and ↓ , inf. n. taHoqiyqN , signifies Sad~aqahu [as meaning he verified it, or proved it to be true or veritable

2 , inf. n. taHoqiyqN : see Haq~ahu , above, in six places. [Hence taHoqiyqu Alhamozapi The uttering of the hemzeh with its ture, or proper, sound; opposed to taxofiyfuhaA . Hence also] Sabagotu Alv~awoba SabogFA taHoqiyqFA I dyed the garment, or piece of cloth, with a saturating dyeing. (TA.) And taHoqiyqN signifies also The weaving a garment, or piece of cloth, strongly, or firmly. (KL.) -A2- Hq~q fiY A^amorihi He was serious, or in earnest, in his affair; contr. of hazala . (L in art. jd .)

3 , (S, K,) inf. n. HiqaAqN and muHaAq~apN , (TA,) He disputed, litigated, or contended, with him, (S, K,) each of them laying claim to a right, or due: (S, TA:) the verb is mostly used in the third person. (TA.) You say, HaAq~aniY wa lamo yuHaAq~aniY fiyhi A^aHadN [ He disputed, &c., with me, and no one had disputed, &c., with me respecting it ]. (TA.) [But] you say also, ↓ I disputed, litigated, or contended, with him for a right, or due, and I overcame him in doing so. (TA.) And A_in~ahu lanaziqu AlHiqaAqi (tropical:) Verily he is one who disputes, or litigates, or contends, respecting small things. (S, K, TA.) And maA lahu fiyhi Haq~N wa laA HiqaAqN , i. e. [ He has no right, or due, to exact, in respect of him, or it, nor any cause of] disputing, or litigating, or contending. (S.) And
; or it is pl. of ↓ . (TA. [See art. nS ; in which this trad. is more fully, but somewhat differently, cited; and fully explained.]) -A2- [
Also, app., He acted seriously, or in earnest, with him in an affair: see
3 in art. jd : and see also
2 above, last signification.]

4 , [inf. n. A_iHoqaAqN ,] He spoke truth; said what was true: [very common in this sense; contr. of A^aboTala :] or he revealed, or manifested, or showed, a truth, or a right or due: or he laid claim to a right, (or to a thing, TA) and it was, or became, due to him. (Msb.) -A2- See also Haq~a , as an intrans. verb, in three places; relating to camels. ― -b2- AHq~ Alqawomu The people's cattle became fat. (TA.) And AHq~ Alqawomu mina Alr~abiyEi The people's cattle became fat by means of the [ herbage called ] rbyE . (AHn, * ISd, TA.) -A3- As a trans. verb: see Haq~ahu , in nine places. You say also, A^aHoqaqotu AlA^amora , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) I did, performed, or executed, the affair in a firm, solid, sound, or good, manner

; or put it into a firm, solid, sound, or good, state. (TA.) ― -b2- ramaY faA^aHaq~a Alr~amiy~apa (tropical:) He cast, or shot, and killed on the spot the animal at which he cast, or shot. (Ibn-'Abbád, Z, K, * TA.) ― -b3- A^aHaq~ato A_ibilunaA rabiyEFA and ↓ rbyEA (assumed tropical:) Our camels found [ herbage such as is termed ] rbyE full-grown, and pastured upon it. (TA.)

5 [ It was, or became, or proved to be, a truth, a reality, or a fact. ] [Hence,] tHq~q Einodahu Alxabaru The information was, or proved, true, right, correct, or valid, in his estimation. (S, K. *) -A2- tHq~qhu : see Haq~ahu .

6 is syn. with taxaASumN ; and ↓ , with AixotiSaAmN ; [The disputing, litigating, or contending, together; ] (S, K;) [for] taxaASamuwA and AixotaSamuwA signify the same; (K in art. xSm ;) [or rather] the meaning of [ tHAq~ and] ↓ is [the disputing, &c., together for a right, or due; ] each one's, or every one's, saying, “ The right is mine, ” and “ with me; ” or demanding his right, or due. (TA.) One says, taHaAq~NwA [ They disputed, &c., together for a right, or due ]. (TK.) And ↓ They two disputed, &c., (K, TA,) each of them demanding his right, or due. (TA.) And fulaAnN wa fulaAnN ↓ [ Such a one and such a one disputed, &c., together for a right, or due ]. (S.) One does not say of a single person [ tHAq~ nor] ↓ ; like as one does not say of one only [ txASm nor] AxtSm . (S.)
7 (tropical:) The knot became tied, or made fast, or tightened. (Ibn-' Abbád, K, TA.)

8 see 6, throughout. -A2- AiHotaq~ato bihi AlT~aEonapu (assumed tropical:) The thrust, or piercing, killed him: (AA, K:) or (tropical:) went right, or directly, into him: (As, TA:) or (assumed tropical:) penetrated into his belly, or inside: (L, TA:) or hit, or struck, the socket, or turning-place, of his hip, which is termed its Huq~ . (K, * TA.) One says, ramaY fulaAnN AlS~ayoda faA@Hotaq~a baEoDFA wa $ar~ama baEoDFA (assumed tropical:) Such a one shot, or cast, at the objects of the chase, and killed some, and wounded some so that they escaped: (S:) or pierced into the bellies, or insides, of some, and wounded the skin of some without so piercing. (L.) -A3- AHtq~hu A_ilaY ka*aA He kept him, or held him, back, or retarded him, [ until such a time, or such an event, ] and straitened him.
; or slender, and lean
; or lean, and lank in the belly. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- And AHtq~ AlmaAlu The cattle became fat: (K: [see also the last meaning of
1 as an intrans. verb:]) but in the A and O and L, AHtq~ Alqawomu the people's cattle became fat, and their fatness ended, or attained the extreme point. (TA.)

10 He demanded it as his right, or due. (TA.) [And hence,] He had a right, or just title or claim, to it; he was, or became, entitled to it; he deserved it, or merited it; syn. Aisotawojabahu : (S, Msb, K:) or these two verbs are nearly the same; (TA;) [the former meaning he was, or became, adapted, disposed, apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, competent, or proper, for it; which is the most proper meaning of the phrase SaAra HaqiyqFA bihi , as well as of the verb AstHq~ ; but this verb has also the former of these two meanings.] When a man purchases a house, and another lays claim to it, and establishes a just evidence of his claim, and the judge decides for him according to his evidence, one says of him, qadi A@sotaHaq~ahaA EalaY Almu$otariY [ He has a right to it in preference to

Hence, It (an action, and anything,) deserved it, merited it, or required it. ] And AstHq~ A_ivomFA He did what necessitated sin; (Ksh and Bd and Jel in v. 106;) [ was guilty of a sin; ] and deserved its being said of him that he was a sinner; (Ksh ibid.;) i. q. Aisotawojabahu . (TA.) And AstHq~wA They committed sins for which he who should punish them would be excusable, because they deserved punishment; like A^awojabuwA , and A^aEo*aruwA , and AisotalaATuwA . (IAar, TA in art. lwT .) ― -b3- AstHq~t A_ibilunaA rabiyEFA : see 4, last sentence. ― -b4- AstHq~t Aln~aAqapu laqaAHFA The she-camel conceived, or became pregnant; and AstHq~ laqaAHuhaA [signifies the same]. (TA.) ― -b5- See also 1, as an intrans. verb, last two sentences.

1 , inf. n. HaqoHaqapN , He went the pace, or in the manner, termed HaqoHaqapN ; (TA;) which means a pace, or manner of going, in which the beast is made to exert himself to the very utmost, and which is the most fatiguing to the Zahor [meaning the camel that is ridden, or the beast that carries one ]: (S, Mgh, K:) or a journeying in the beginning, or first part, of the night; (Lth, S, K;) which is forbidden: (Lth, S, TA:) or, as some say, the fatiguing a while, and abstaining a while: (Lth, TA:) but Az says that Lth is not correct in either of his explanations of this word: (TA:) or an obstinate persisting in journeying: or an obstinate persisting in journeying until the camel that one is riding perishes or breaks down: (K:) or, accord. to Az, the correct meaning, confirmed by what the Ar

contr. of baATilN [used as a subst. and as an epithet or act. part. n.]: (S, Msb, K:) or, as an inf. n. [and used as a simple subst.], contr. of buTolaAnN ; and as an act. part. n., and a simple epithet, contr. of baATilN . (Kull.) [As a subst.,] its primary signification is Suitableness to the requirements of wisdom, justice, right, or rightness, truth, reality, or fact

; or to the exigencies of the case; as the suitableness of the foot of a door in respect of its socket, for turning round rightly: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [and particularly] the suitableness of a judgment, and of what involves, or implies, a judgment, [i. e., of a saying, and a religion, and a persuasion, or the like, (as will be shown by one of the explanations of its meanings as an epithet,)] to reality or fact; and the suitableness of reality or fact to a judgment: (Kull:) [the state, or quality, or property, of being just, proper, right, correct, or true; justness, propriety, rightness, correctness, or truth; reality, or fact; the state, &c., of being established, or confirmed, as a truth or fact; of being necessary, requisite, or unavoidable; of being binding, obligatory, incumbent, or due:

139.) [Respecting the expressions AlHaq~u Alyaqiynu and Haq~u Alyaqiyni , see art. yqn .] ― -b2- [From the primary and general signification, explained in the first sentence of this paragraph, are deduced several particular meanings here following.] ― -b3- Equity, or justice. (K.) ― -b4- [The right mode, or manner, of acting or being. ] ― -b5- Veracity (K) in discourse. (TA.) ― -b6- Prudence. (K, TA.) ― -b7- [ A right, or due, of any kind: a just claim: a desert, or thing deserved: anything that is owed; as a fee, hire, or pay, and a price: a duty; an obligation: ] the sing. of HuquwqN . (S, K.) [You say, h`*aA Haq~iY This is my right, or due, &c. And h`*aA Haq~N liY This is a right, or due, belonging to me

; or a thing due, or owed, to me: or this is a duty to me. And h`*aA Haq~N EalaY~a This is a right, or due, the rendering of which is binding, obligatory, or incumbent, on me: or this is my duty. And hence, Haq~u AlT~ariyqi The duty that relates to the road: see art. Trq .] ↓ is a more particular, or peculiar, or special, term. (S, K.) You say, ↓ [ This is my particular, or peculiar, or special, right or due &c.: but it is explained as] meaning Haq~iY . (S.) And ↓ This is my just, or necessary, or incumbent, right or due &c. (K.) ― -b8- A share, or portion; as in the saying, A^aEoTi kul~a *iY Haq~K Haq~ahu Give thou to every one to whom belongs a share, or portion, his share, or portion, that is appointed, or assigned, to him. (TA.) ― -b9- Property: a possession. (K.) ― -b10- [ An apperten

1. 18], where it is said, wa jaA='ato sakorapu Almawoti biAlHaq~i [ And the confusion of the intellect by reason of the agony of death shall come with death: but other and obvious meanings are assigned to it in this instance]. (TA.) ― -b14- [As an epithet,] AlHaq~u is one of the names of God: or one of the epithets applied to Him: (K:) meaning the Really-existing; whose existence and divinity are proved to be true: (IAth, TA:) or the Creator according to the requirements of wisdom, justice, right, or rightness. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b15- It is also applied to The Kur-án. (K.) ― -b16- And to [ The religion of ] El-Islám. (K.) -A2- See also HaqiyqN , in two places. -A3- And see HaAq~N , in two places.

: see Huq~apN . ― -b2- Also The breast, or mamma, of an old woman. (TA.) ― -b3- A tuber of a truffle. (TA.) ― -b4- The small hollow upon the head of the shoulder-blade: (K:) or, as some say, the Huq~ of the shoulder-blade is the head of the upper arm, in which is the waAbilap : (TA:) or this latter is another signification of Huq~ . (K.) ― -b5- The head, (K,) or lower part of the head, (TA,) of the hip, in which is the thigh-bone; (K, TA;) the socket, or turning-place, of the hip. (TA.) ― -b6- The socket, or turning-place, of the foot of a door. (TA.) You say, laqiytuhu Einoda Huq~i baAbi Almasojidi , meaning I met him, or found him, near to the mosque: and Almasojidi ↓ [app. means the same]. (TA.) ― -b7- See also HaAq~N , in two places. ― -b8- Also The web of a spider. (Az, K.)

A camel three years old, (S, Mgh,) that has entered the fourth year: (S, Mgh, Msb:) or a camel entering the fourth year: (K:) so called because fit to be laden (S, Msb) and made use of; (S;) or because fit to be ridden

; or because fit for covering: (K:) the female is termed ↓ , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and Hiq~N also: (S, K:) the pl. (of Hiq~N , Msb) is HiqaAqN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and (of Hiq~apN , Msb) HiqaqN , (Msb, K,) and the pl. pl., (K,) i. e. pl. of HiqaAqN , (S,) is HuquqN , (S, K,) and sometimes HaqaAy^iqu , (S, TA,) or this is a pl. of Hiq~apN . (TA: see

3.) Or [so in the K, but it should rather be “ and, ”] Hiq~N signifies A she-camel whose teeth have fallen out by reason of extreme age. (K.) ― -b2- One says, raA^ayotahaA wa hiYa Hiq~apN as meaning (assumed tropical:) [ I saw her when she was ] like a she-camel termed Hq~p in bigness. (TA.) ― -b3- And [the pl.] HiqaAqN is applied to The young ones of trees: (TA:) and particularly of the [species of mimosa termed] EurofuT : (K, TA:) as being likened to the camels termed HqAq . (TA.) -A2- Also (tropical:) The time of year in which a she-camel was covered in the preceding year; (S, TA;) and so ↓ : (TA:) or the usual period of her gestation. (L in art. nDj .) You say, A^atati Aln~aAqapu EalaY Hiq~ihaA (tropical:) The she-camel arrived at the time of year in which she had been covered in the p

; or she completed her period of gestation, and overpassed by some days the time of year in which she had been covered in the preceding year, to complete the formation of the fœtus. (TA.) And jaAzati AlHiq~a She (a camel) overpassed the year without bringing forth. (As, S.) [See also the last sentence but one in the explanations of
1 as an intrans. verb.] ― -b2- kaAna *`lika Einoda Hiq~i laqaAHihaA : see Haq~N
: see Haq~N , in two places: ― -b2- and HaqiyqapN , also in two places: ― -b3- and HaAq~apN .

A receptacle of wood, (K, TA,) or of ivory, or of some other material proper to be cut, or shaped out; (TA;) a receptacle for perfume; (Har p. 518;) [generally a small round box, used for unguents and perfumes &c.; and applied also to a small cocoa-nut used as a box for snuff &c.;] a thing well known: (S:) [also a receptacle for wine: (see taA^omuwrN , in art. Amr :)] pl. ↓ , [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., as is indicated in the TA, and it is now used as a sing., like Huq~apN ,] and HuqaqN , (S, K,) which latter is pl. of Huq~apN , (ISd, TA,) and HiqaAqN (S, K) and HuquwqN and [of pauc.] A^aHoqaAqN , (K,) which three are pls. of Huq~N . (TA.) ― -b2- And (tropical:) A woman; (K, TA;) as being likened thereto. (TA.) -A2- See also HaAq~apN .
: see h`*ihi Hiq~atiY , voce Haq~N . -A2- See also Hiq~N , in three places.

, in a horse, The quality of not sweating: (S, * K:) which is a fault. (TA.) ― -b2- And, in a horse also, The putting down the hind hoof in the place [ that has just before been that ] of the fore hoof: (S, * K:) which is also a fault. (K.) [See A^aHaq~u .]

[app. pl. of the act. part. n. HaAq~N , like buzulN pl. of baAzilN , &c.,] Persons who have recently known, or been acquainted with, events, or affairs, good and evil. (TA.) ― -b2- And Persons establishing a claim or claims. (TA.)

Adapted, disposed, apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, proper, competent, or worthy; syn. xaliyqN , (Sh, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and jadiyrN ; (K;) as also ↓ , (Ibn- 'Abbád, K,) and [some say] ↓ : (Sh, S, Mgh, K:) HaqiyqN is said to be of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; but accord. to the A, it is not so, because its fem. is with p ; but is from the supposed verb Haquqa , and is like xaliyqN from xaluqa , and jadiyrN from jadura : and ↓ signifies [properly] rendered adapted &c.: (TA:) the pl. of Hqyq is A^aHiq~aA='u ; and that of ↓ is maHoquwquwna . (S.) You say, huwa HaqiyqN bihi (Sh, S, Msb, K) and bh ↓ (Sh, S, K) and bh ↓ (Ibn-'Abbád, K) [ He is adapted, &c., for it
; or worthy of it ]. And to a woman, A^anota HaqiyqapN bika*aA (A, TA) and HaqiyqapN li*`lika and li*`lika ↓ [ Thou art adapted, &c., for such a thing and for that thing
; or worthy of it ]. (TA.) And A^anota HaqiyqN biA^ano tafoEala (A, Mgh) and ↓ (A) [ Thou art adapted, &c., for thy doing such a thing
; or worthy of doing it]. And huwa HaqiyqN A^ano yafoEala ka*aA [ He is adapted, &c., for his doing such a thing

; or worthy to do it ]; (S;) in which case, An is for biA^ano . (Mgh.) [And HaqiyqN bika*aA also signifies Having a right, or just title or claim, to such a thing; entitled to such a thing. ] It is said in the Kur [vii. 103], HaqiyqN EalaY A^ano laA A^aqowla EalaY A@ll~`hi A_il~aA AlHaq~a , meaning I am disposed [ not ] to say [ of God aught save ] the truth: or, as some say, I am vehemently desirous [ that I should not say &c.]; for, accord. to Aboo-'Alee, A^anaA HaqiyqN EalaY ka*aA means I am vehemently desirous of such a thing: but one reading, that of Náfi', is HaqiyqN EalaY~a A^ano laA A^aquwla , It is binding, or obligatory, or incumbent, on me [ that I should not say ]. The essence of a thing as meaning that by being which a thing is what it is; [or that in being which a thing consists; ] as when we say that a rational animal is the Hqyqp of a human being: (KT:) or that by being which a thing is what it is, considered with regard to its reality, is termed HaqiyqapN : considered with regard to its individuality, huwiy~apN : and without regard thereto, maAhiy~apN : (KT, TA:) the ultimate and radical constituent of a thing. Hak~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) [ He scratched, scraped, rubbed, grated, chafed, or fretted, it: or] he scraped off, abraded, or otherwise removed, its superficial part: (Mgh, Msb:) Hak~N signifies the act of scratching: (KL:) or the making a body to pass upon another body with collision: (K:) [as meaning scratching and the like,] it is with the nail, and with the hand, &c. (TA.) maA Hak~a ZahoriY mivolu yadiY [ Nothing has scratched my back like my hand ] is a prov., meaning that one should abstain from relying upon others: and the same meaning is intended in the following verse: maA Hak~a jilodaka mivolu Zuforiko fataw~ala A^anota jamiyEa A^amoriko [ Nothing has scratched thy skin like thy nail: so manage thou thyself all thine affair ]. (Har pp.

432 et seq.) The saying, in a trad., A_i*aA Hakakotu qaroHapF dam~ayotuhaA [lit. When I scratch a sore, I make it bleed, ] means (tropical:) when I desire an object, I attain it. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Hak~a fiY SadoriY , and ↓ , and ↓ , (K,) the first whereof, which is mentioned by IDrd preceded by the negative maA , is the most approved, (TA,) (tropical:) It wrought, or operated, in, or upon, my mind: (K, TA:) said of a suggestion of the devil, that comes into one's mind. (TA.) Or Hak~a fiY Sadorihi ka*aA , aor. , means (assumed tropical:) Such a thing occurred to his mind as a thing outweighed in probability, or a matter of suspicion. (Msb.) And you say maA Hak~a fiY SadoriY (assumed tropical:) It did not make an impression upon my mind. (Har p.

648.) It is said in a trad., AlA_ivomu maA Hak~a fiY Sadorika (assumed tropical:) Sin is that which makes an impression upon thy mind, and induces a suspicion that it is an act of disobedience, because the mind is not dilated thereby. (Mgh. [See also HaAka , in arts. Hwk and Hyk ; and see Haz~a .]) You say also, maA Hak~a fiY SadoriY minohu $aYo'N (tropical:) Nothing thereof was unsettled, so as to be doubtful, in my mind. (S, TA.) And maA Hak~a fiY SadoriY ka*aA (tropical:) Such a thing did not cause dilatation [or pleasure ] in my mind. (S, K, TA.) -A2- See also

[The pigeon, both wild and domestic, but more properly the former; and sometimes not strictly confined to denote the pigeon-kind:] a certain wild bird, that does not keep to the houses; well-known: (ISd, K:) or any collared, or ringed, bird; (S, Msb, K;) so with the Arabs; such as the fawaAxit and the qamaAriY~ and saAqu Hur~ and the qaTaA and the waraA$iyn and the like, (S, Msb,) and the domestic [ pigeons ] ( Ald~awaAjin ), also, (El-Umawee, S, Msb,) that are taken into houses for the purpose of producing their young ones; (El-Umawee, S;) to which last alone the term is applied by the vulgar: accord. to Ks, it is the wild [ species ]; and the yamaAm is that which keeps to the houses: accord. to As, the latter is the HamaAm waHo$iY~ [or wild pigeon ]; a species of the birds of the desert:

The fever ( Hum~aY ) of camels; (S;) as also ↓ : (TA:) or of all beasts, (K, TA,) including camels: (TA:) accord. to ISh, when camels eat date-stones, [which are often given to them as food,] they are [sometimes] affected with HumaAm and qumaAH ; the former of which is a heat affecting the skin, until the body is smeared with mud, or clay, in consequence of which they forsake the abundant herbage, and their fat goes away; and it continues in them a month, and then passes away. (Az, TA.) ― -b2- HumaAmu qur~K The disease termed muwm , which affects men. (TA.) ― -b3- See also HamiymN . -A2- A noble chief, or lord: (K:) thought by Az to be originally humaAmN . (TA.)
: see its syn. Hum~apN ; of which it is also a pl. (K.)

One says, (to a person who has been in the bath, A, TA,) TaAba Hamiymuka and ↓ , meaning May thy sweat be good, or pleasant; (Az, A, K;) and consequently, may God make thy body sound, or healthy: (A, TA:) or the former may mean as above, or may thy bathing be good, or pleasant: (IB:) one should not say, ↓ , (K, TA,) though MF defends it. (TA.) -A2- A relation, (Lth, S, K,) for whose case one is anxious or solicitous, (S,) or whom one loves and by whom one is beloved: (Lth, K:) or an affectionate, or a compassionate, relation, who is sharp, or hasty, to protect his kinsfolk: or an object of love; a person beloved: (TA:) or a man's brother; his friend, or true friend; because anxious, or solicitous, for him: (Ham p. 90:) and ↓ signifies the same: the pl. : see HamiymN . ― -b2- Also Heated milk. (K.) -A2-

Also, (S, K,) as well as ↓ , (K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, Hum~ ,]) sing. of HamaAy^imu signifying (tropical:) Such as are held in high estimation, precious, or excellent, or the choice, or best, (S, K, TA,) of cattle or other property, (S,) or of camels: (K:) and accord. to Kr, the sing. is used as a pl. in this sense: (ISd, TA:) ↓ , likewise, signifies the choice, or best, of cattle or other property; and so ↓ , of camels: (K:) or you say A_ibilN HaAm~apN , meaning excellent, or choice, camels. (S.)

; accord. to the K, HumayomaAtN , but this is the pl.; (TA;) A live coal; syn. jamorapN : (K, TA:) or redness; syn. HumorapN : (CK, and so in a MS. copy of the K:) [in Freytag's Lex., the pl. is explained as meaning redness of the skin; and so ↓ .]
: see what next precedes.
One who flies pigeons ( HamaAm ), and sends them [ as carriers of letters ] to various towns or countries. (TA.)

, (S, K, &c.,) a subst. from Hum~ , (Lh, L, K,) imperfectly decl., because of the fem. alif [which terminates it], (Msb,) A fever; a disease by which the body becomes hot: from AlHamiymu : said to be so called because of the excessive heat; whence the trad., AlHum~aY mino fayoHi jahan~ama [ Fever is from the exhalation of Hell ]: or because of the sweat that occurs in it: or because it is of the signs of AlHimaAm [i. e. the decreed, or predestined, case of death]; for they say, AlHum~aY raAy^idu Almawoti [ Fever is the messenger that precedes death ], or bariydu Almawoti [ the messenger of death ], or baAbu Almawoti [ the gate of death ]: (TA:) and ↓ signifies the same: (K, TA:) pl. of the former Hum~ayaAtN . (Msb.)
: see HumaAmN .

[ A hot bath; ] a certain structure, (S,) well known; (Msb;) so called because it occasions sweating, or because of the hot water that is in it; accord. to ISd, derived from AlHamiymu ; (TA;) i. q. dayomaAsN : (K:) of the masc. gender, (Mgh, K,) and fem. also, (Mgh,) generally the latter; (Msb;) but some say that it is a mistake to make it fem., (MF, TA,) though IB cites a verse in which a fem. pronoun is asserted to refer to a Hm~Am : (TA:) pl. Ham~aAmaAtN ; (S, Mgh, K;) accord. to Sb, [not because the sing. is fem., but] because, though masc., it has no broken pl. (TA.) See also HamiymN .
The owner [or keeper ] of a Ham~aAm [or hot bath ]. (Mgh.)
: see A^aHam~u .
: see A^aHam~u , in two places.

The xaAS~ap [or particular, or special, friends, or familiars ], (S, K,) consisting of the family and children (K) and relations, (TA,) of a man. (K.) You say, kayofa AlHaAm~apu waAlEaAm~apu [ How are the particular, or special, friends, &c., and the common people? ]. (S.) And h`w^ulaA='i HaAm~apu Alr~ajuli These are the relations of the man. (Lth, S.) [See Hum~apN , and A^aHm~u .] ― -b2- See also HamiymapN . ― -b3- Also i. q. EaAm~apN . (K.) [It would seem that this signification might have been assigned to it in consequence of a misunderstanding of the words in the S, waAlHaAm~apu AlxaAS~apu yuqaAlu kayofa AlHaAm~apu waAlEaAm~apu : but accord. to the TK, one says, jaAw^uwA HaAm~apF , meaning EaAm~apF , i. e. They came generally, or universally. ]

and *awaAtu HaAmiyma , (K,) or ↓ and *awaAtu H`m= , (S,) A=l being prefixed in this case in like manner as in A=lu fulaAnK , (Fr, S,) Certain chapters of the Kur-án (S, K) commencing with HAmym [or H`m= ], (K,) [namely, the fortieth and six following chapters, ] called by Ibn-Mes'ood diybaAju AlquroA=ni : (S:) one should not say HawaAmiym : (K:) this is vulgar: (S:) but it occurs in poetry. (S, K.) ― -b2-

Also, (K,) accord. to I'Ab, ↓ is One of the names of God; (Mgh;) or it is the most great name of God; (K;) occurring in a trad., in which it is said, A_ino buy~it~umo faquwluwA H`m= laA yanoSaruwna , meaning If ye be attacked by night, say ye H`m= ; and when ye say this, they shall not be made victorious: (Mgh:) or the meaning is, [ say ye ] O God, they shall not be made victorious; not being an imprecation; for were it so, it would be laA yunoSaruwA : (IAth, TA:) or it is an oath; (Mgh, K;) and the meaning of the trad. is, [say ye] By God, they shall not be made victorious: but H`m= is not among the numbered names of God: it has therefore been deemed preferable to understand it as here meaning the seven chapters of the Kur-án commencing therewith: (Mgh:) or it is an abbreviation of Alr~aH
; or because it is of a foreign measure, like qaAbiylu and haAbiylu , (Ksh, Bd,) and determinate. (Ksh.)

Black; (S, K;) applied to anything; as also ↓ , (K,) and ↓ , (As, K,) or this signifies intensely black, (S,) and ↓ , (K,) which IB explains as a black hue of dye: (TA:) [the fem. of the first is Ham~aA='u : and the pl. Hum~N : and] the pl. of ↓ the second is yaHaAmiymu , and by poetic license yaHaAmimu . (Sb, TA.) You say, rajulN A^aHam~u A black man. (S.) And rajulN A^aHam~u Almuqolatayoni A man having black eyes. (TA.) And kumayotN A^aHam~u [ A blackish bay horse]: pl. kumotN Hum~N ; which are the strongest of horses in skin and hoofs. (S.) And ↓ A black sheep or goat. (TA.) And layolN A^aHam~u Black night. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AlHam~aA='u The anus ( saAfilap , S, or Aisot , K) of a human being: (S:) pl. Hum~N . (S, K.) ― -b3- And A^aHam~u An arrow before it has been furnished with fea
: see maHam~apN : -A2- and see also HamiymN .

i. q. qumoqumapN : (Mgh, Msb;) i. e. A vessel of copper [or brass ], in which water is heated, (KL, and Msb in art. qm ,) having a long and narrow neck: (KL:) or a small qumoqum [here meaning the same as qumoqumap ], in which water is heated. (S.)
, applied to food [&c.], (TA,) Any cause of fever

; or a thing from the eating of which one is affected with fever: (K, * TA:) such, for instance, the eating of fresh ripe dates is said to be. (TA.) And A^aroDN maHam~apN (S, M, K) and ↓ , (M, K,) mentioned by AAF, but not known by the lexicologists except as agreeable with analogy, [see its verb, 4,] (M, TA,) A land in which is fever: (S, K:) or in which is much fever. (K.)
Fevered, or affected with fever, or sick of a fever. (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) -A2- Applied to water, like mavomuwdN [q. v.]. (Az, TA.) -A3- Decreed, or appointed. (S, TA.)
Keeping constantly, firmly, steadily, steadfastly, or fixedly, EalaY A^amorK to an affair. (AZ, K. *)
, (TA,) or musotaHam~apN , (Mgh,) A place in which one washes with hot water. (Mgh, * TA.)

: see A^aHam~u , in two places. ― -b2- Also Smoke: (S, M, K:) or black smoke: (Bd in lvi. 42:) or intensely black smoke. (Jel ibid. and TA.) ― -b3- A black mountain: (K:) or a certain black mountain in Hell. (TA.) ― -b4- The canopy, or awning, that is extended over the people of Hell: so, as some say, in the Kur lvi.
42. (TA.) ― -b5- A certain bird: (K:) so called because of the blackness of its wings. (TA.) ― -b6- nabotN yaHomuwmN A plant, or herbage, green, full of moisture, and black. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. Hamo'N , (S,) He cleansed the well of its HamoA^ap [or black, fetid mud ]. (S, K.) In the T, this signification is assigned to Alby^r ↓ ; and the signification assigned below to the latter is given to HmA^ : but As says that he does not find this authorized by usage. (TA.) -A2- Hamiy^a , aor. , inf. n. Hamo'N and HamaA^N , It (water) was, or became, mixed with black, fetid mud, and so rendered turbid, (K, TA,) and altered in odour. (TA.) And Hamiy^ati Albiy^oru , inf. n. HamaA^N , The well had in it black [ fetid ] mud (S, Msb) in abundance: (S:) and the like is also said of a spring. (TA.) -A3- Hamiy^a Ealayohi He was angry with him; (El-Umawee, S, K;) as also HamiYa . (Lh, TA.)
4 , (ISk, S, K,) inf. n. A_iHomaA='N , (ISk, S,) He threw HamoA^ap [or black, fetid mud ] into the well. (ISk, S, K.) ― -b2- See also

and HamN and Hamuw [only used as a prefixed n. governing the gen. case (see HamN in art. Hmw )] and HamFA (S, Msb, K) and ↓ (K) A woman's husband's father; (IF, Msb, K;) and a man's wife's father: (IF, Msb:) or a man's wife's father or wife's brother or wife's paternal uncle: (M, Msb:) or any one of a woman's husband's [ male ] relations, (S, O, K,) as the brother and the father (S, O) and the paternal uncle; (O, TA;) and of a man's wife's relations: (K:) pl. A^aHomaA='N : (S, K:) the fem. is HamaAopN . (TA.) -A2- See also HamoA^apN .
: see Hamo'N : -A2- and see also what next follows.

(S, Msb, K) and ↓ , (S, K,) but accord. to some, the latter is the pl. [or rather quasipl. n.] of the former; and sometimes, by poetic license, it is written ↓ ; (TA;) Black mud: (S, Msb:) or black fetid mud. (K.) -A2-
Also, the former, A certain plant, (K,) that grows in Nejd, in the sands, and in plain, or soft, land. (TA.)

A man of an evil eye, (Fr, K,) who injures with his eye him whom he sees and admires: no verb belonging to it has been heard. (Fr, TA.) -A2- Hamiy^apN A well ( biy^or ) or a spring ( Eayon ) foul with black, fetid mud. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. HamodN (S, L, Msb, K) and maHomadN and maHomidN (L, K) and maHomadapN (S, L, K) and maHomidapN ; (L, K, and so in a copy of the S;) the last of these inf. ns. [and the third also] extr.; (L;) or the last is an inf. n. and the last but one signifies “ a praiseworthy quality, ” or “ a quality for which one is praised; ” (ElFenáree, MF;) or the last may be a simple subst.; (Har p. 392;) He praised, eulogized, or commended, him; spoke well of him; mentioned him with approbation; (Akh, S, L, Msb;) EalaY ka*aA for such a thing; (L, Msb;) contr. of *am~ahu : (S, L:) accord. to IAmb, formed by transposition from madaHa : (marginal note in a copy of the MS:) but it is of less common application than the latter verb; (Msb in art. mdH ;) signifying he praised him, &c., for somethin

; or I praise to thee God's blessings, or favours, and discourse to thee of them. (L.) And Hamida lahu A^amorFA (tropical:) He approved of a thing for him. (L, K. *) And Hamida A_ilayohi A^amorFA (tropical:) He approved of a thing for him, and commanded, or enjoined, him to do it. (L.) And jAwarotuhu famaA Hamidotu jiwaArahu (tropical:) [ I became his neighbour, and did not approve of being so ]. (A.) See also

Also, (aor. and inf. n. as above in the beginning of this art., K,) He recompensed, or requited, him: he gave him, or paid him, his due. (L, K.) -A2- Hamida Ealayohi , aor. , (L, K, *) inf. n. HamadN , (TA,) He was angry with him. (L, K.)

2 , inf. n. taHomiydN , has a more intensive signification than Hamda ; (S;) [ He declared the praises of God: or] he praised God much, with good forms of praise ( biAlmaHaAmidi AlHasanapi ): (T, L:) or repeatedly
; or time after time. (L, K.) tHmyd [used as a simple subst.] has a pl., namely, taHaAmiydu . (A.) [See an ex. voce xaAtamN , in the latter part of the paragraph.]

4 He (a man, S) came to a state, or result, such as was praised, or commended, or approved; properly, his affair, or case, came to such a state or result: (S, L, K:) or (so in the K, but in the L “ and ”) he did, or said, that for which he should be praised, or commended

; or that which was praiseworthy, or commendable; (A, L, K; *) contr. of A^a*am~a . (A.) And AHmd A^amoruhu (assumed tropical:) His affair, or case, was, or became, praiseworthy, or approvable, in his estimation: (K:) or AHmd A^amorahu (as in the L) he esteemed his affair, or case, praiseworthy, or approvable. (L [agreeably with what next follows].) -A2- AHmdhu He found him (a man, A, L) [or it ] to be such as is praised, commended, or approved

; or praiseworthy, commendable, or approvable; (S, A, L, Msb;) contr. of A^a*am~ahu : (TA in art. *m :) he made it manifest that he was worthy of praise, eulogy, commendation, or approbation: (L:) he approved of his action, and his course of conduct, or his tenet or tenets, and did not expose it, or them, to others. (K.) And A^aHomadotu SaniyEahu (tropical:) [ I found his action to be praiseworthy, or commendable, or approvable ]. (A.) And AHmd AlA^aroDa (tropical:) He approved the land as a dwelling-place: (A:) or he found the land to be such as is praised, commended, or approved; as also ↓ ; (L, K;) but the former verb is the more chaste in this sense. (L.) And AHmd mawoDiEFA (tropical:) He found a place to be such as is praised, commended, or approved, and convenient, or suitable, so th

5 He affected, or made a show of, ( takal~afa ,) praise. (A.) You say, ↓ muta$ak~irFA [ I found him affecting, or making a show of, praise and thanks ]. (A.) ― -b2- He praised himself. (KL.) [Golius assigns this meaning to ↓ , as on the authority of the KL; but it is not assigned to this verb in my copy of the KL.] ― -b3- fulaAnN yataHam~adu Aln~As [app. a slight mistranscription, for liln~aAsi , i. q. A_ilaY Aln~aAsi , as in an ex. in the next sentence but one,] Such a one pretends to men, or shows them, that he is praiseworthy, bijuwdihi for his liberality. (L.) ― -b4- tHm~d Ealayohi He reproached him for a favour, or benefit, which he (the former) had bestowed, or conferred

; or recounted his gifts, or actions, to him; syn. Aimotan~a . (S, L, K.) One says, mano A^anofaqa maAlahu EalaY nafosihi falaA yataHam~ado bihi EalaY Aln~aAsi [ Whoso expends his property upon himself, he shall not reproach men therewith as for favours, or benefits, bestowed ]: (S, A:) or flA ytHm~d bih A_ilaY Aln~aAsi [ he shall not pretend to men that he is praiseworthy on account of it ]: a prov., meaning that a man is not praised for his beneficence to himself, but for his beneficence to others. (L.)
6 (tropical:) [ They praised, or commended, a thing, one to another ]. You say, Alr~uEaA='u yataHaAmaduwna AlkalaA^a (tropical:) [ The pastors praise, or commend, one to another, the herbage ]. (A.)
5. -A2- Said of heat, [ It burned, or burned fiercely
; or was, or became, vehement: ] formed by transposition from AHtdm . (S.)

senses.text: 10 Ealayohimo [so I find it written, as though meaning Demand thou, of his creatures, the praising of God, by reason of his beneficence to them, and his bounty to them: but I think that we should read AisotaHomada A@ll~`hu , and that the meaning is, God hath demanded praise of his creatures by his beneficence, &c.]. (A.)

Praise, eulogy, or commendation; &c. (S, &c. [For further explanations of this word, and respecting the phrase AlHamodu lil~`hi and its variations, see 1: and see also $akara .]) suboHaAnaka A@ll~`hum~a wabiHamodika , said by a person praying, means [ I extol, or celebrate, or declare, thy remoteness, or freedom, from every impurity, or imperfection, &c., O God, (see art. sbH ,)] and I begin with praising Thee; A^abotadiy^u being understood: (Az, L, Msb:) or by bHmdk is meant AlHamodu laka praise be to Thee: and nearly the same is said in explanation of the phrase in the Kur [ii. 28], nusab~iHu biHamodika , that by bHmdk is meant HaAmidiyna laka : [see, again, art. sbH :] or by the expression wbHmdk is meant, accord. to Aboo-'Othmán ElMázinee, and by praising Thee I extol thy remoteness, o

: see Ham~aAdN .

Praise, and thanks, be to him: (S, L, K:) i. e., to such a one: (S, L:) contr. of jamaAdi lahu [q. v.]. (S and A in art. jmd .) HamaAdi is indecl., with kesr for its termination, because it deviates from its original, which is the inf. n. [↓ ]: (S, L:) [i. e.,] it is [a quasi-inf. n., (see Aisomu maSodarK in art. Sdr ,) being] a proper name for AlmaHomadapu [as syn. with AlHamodu ]. (Sharh Shudhoor edh-Dhahab.)
: see what next follows.

and ↓ (S, A, L, K) and ↓ (as in copies of the K, but this seems to be an intensive epithet,) Praised, eulogized, or commended; spoken well of; mentioned with approbation; approved; such as is praised, &c.; praiseworthy, laudable; commendable, or approvable: (S, L, K: [in which, as well as in numberless exs., all these significations are clearly indicated, though not so clearly explained; the Arabic words to which they apply exactly agreeing with the Latin “ laudatus, ” which means both “ praised ” and “ praiseworthy: ”]) the fem. of the first is with p , (L, K,) because the signification, though properly that of a pass. part. n., nearly agrees with that of an act. part. n.: (L:) you say, [ hiYa HamiydapN She is praised, &c.; and] A^afoEaAluhu HamiydapN (tropical:) [ His actions are praised

(S, L, K *) and ↓ (L) The utmost of thy power, or of thine ability, [or the utmost of thy praiseworthy actions, (see an ex. of the pl. in what follows,) will be ] thy doing such a thing; syn. mabolagu jahodika , (L,) or quSaAraAka , (S, L,) and gaAyatuka : (S, L, K:) and in like manner, HumaAdiY The utmost of my power, &c. senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. HimaAyapN (S, Mgh, K [but said in the Msb to be a simple subst., though afterwards there mentioned as an inf. n.,]) and HamoYN and maHomiyapN , (K,) He prohibited it, or interdicted it

; or he protected it, defended it, or guarded it, from, or against, encroachment, invasion, or attack. (S, * Mgh, K, * TA.) You say, HamaY AlkalaA^a , inf. n. HamoYN and Hamiy~apN and HimaAyapN and HamowapN , [the last irreg.,] He prohibited, or interdicted, &c., the herbage, or pasture. (K, * TA.) And HamaY AlmakaAna mina Aln~aAsi , aor. , inf. n. HamoYN and HimoyapN [and HimaAyapN , though here, in the Msb, said to be a simple subst.], He prohibited, or interdicted, the place

; or he protected, defended, or guarded, it; from the people [ in general ]: (Msb:) and, accord. to IB, ↓ signifies the same as HamaAhu : (TA:) or AlmkAn ↓ signifies he made the place to be what is termed HimFY , (S, Msb, K,) not to be approached (Msb, K) nor ventured upon, or attempted: (Msb:) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (Msb,) he found it to be what is termed HimFY : (Msb, K:) or AlHimaY ↓ signifies he made the HmY to be refrained from by people, and to be acknowledged as a HmY : and HamaAhu , he prohibited, or interdicted, it

; or he protected it, defended it, or guarded it, from, or against, encroachment, invasion, or attack: (AZ:) accord. to Suh, in the R, ↓ is of weak authority; but both these verbs are chaste. (TA.) [Hence,] HamaY Zahorahu [ He prohibited, or interdicted, his back to be used for bearing a rider or any burden], said of a stallion-camel when he is termed HaAmK , q. v. (Fr, S, K.) You say also, HamaAhu mina Al$~aYo'i and HamaAhu Al$~aYo'a [ He protected, defended, or guarded, him from the thing ]. (TA.) And Eanohu ↓ , inf. n. muHaAmaApN and HimaA='N , (S, K,) I protected, defended, or guarded, him. (K.) One says, Eano waladihaA ↓ [ The biting she-camel defends her offspring ]. (S.) And fulaAnN EiroDahu ↓ [ Such a one defended his honour, or reputation ]. (TA.) And Hamayotu Alqawoma , inf. n. H

A thing prohibited, or interdicted; (S, K;) as also ↓ and ↓ ; (K;) and not to be approached: (S:) [and, as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant,] a place of herbage, or pasture, (Lth, Mgh, Msb, * TA, and Ham p. 539,) and of water, (Ham ibid.,) prohibited to the people, [i. e. to the public, ] (Lth, Mgh, and Ham ubi suprà,) so that they may not pasture their beasts in it, (Lth, Mgh,) nor approach it, (Mgh, Msb,) nor venture upon it: (Msb:) it was a custom of the noble among the Arabs, in the Time of Ignorance, when he alighted in a district [that pleased him], among his kinsfolk, to incite a dog to bark, and to prohibit for his own special friends or dependents the space throughout which the bark of the dog was heard, so that none else should pasture his beasts there;

HayuwA , (Fr, S,) like xa$uwA , (S,) and Hay~uwA , (Fr, S,) as some say, (S,) aor. yaHoyaA , (S, Msb, K,) and yaHaY~u , (Fr, K,) [like yamal~u , originally yamolalu ,] occurring in poetry, but improper, and disallowed by the Basrees, (Fr,) inf. n. HayaApN [q. v. infrà], (IB, Mgh, Msb,) or HayaA='N , (K,) and HiY~N and HayawaAnN , (IB,) which last has an intensive signification, like its contr. mawataAnN , (Msb,) He, or it, lived

; or was, or became, in the state termed HayaApN , explained below. (S, K.) [The inf. n. HayawaAnN (q. v. infrà) suggests the supposition that HayiYa may be originally Hayiwa ; but I find no authority for this supposition; and if it be the case, this verb presents the only instance of a root of which the medial radical letter is Y and the final w .] ― -b2- HayuwA , said of a people, or company of men, (assumed tropical:) They were, or became, in good condition: (AA, S:) or they were, or became, fat, by having the means of subsistence, baEoda huzaAlK [ after leanness ]. (AZ. [See also

4.]) ― -b3- You say also, Hay~ati Aln~aAru , inf. n. HayaApN and HayaA='N , (assumed tropical:) [ The fire was, or became, alive, or burning, ] like as you say, maAtat . (AHn.) ― -b4- HayiYa AlT~ariyqu (assumed tropical:) The road, or way, was, or became, apparent, or distinct. (K.) One says, A_i*aA HayiYa laka AlT~ariyqu faxu*o yamonapF (assumed tropical:) [ When the road, or way, becomes apparent, or distinct, to thee, take to the right ]. ; or make thee to continue in life; syn. A^aboqaAka ; (Fr, Selemeh Ibn- 'Ásim, K;) as also ↓ ; (Selemeh Ibn-'Ásim, TA;) or Eam~araka : (Aboo-'Othmán El-Mázinee, Mgh, TA:) or may God save thee

23.) ― -b2- Also He said to him Hay~aAka A@ll~`hu , explained above: (Mgh:) originally, he prayed for his life: and then, he prayed for him, absolutely: (Msb:) he saluted him; (K, TA;) and so Hy~Ahu taHiy~apa Almuw^omini : (Lh, TA:) as used in the language of the law, he said to him, salaAmN Ealayoka . (TA.)

4 , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. A_iHoyaA='N , (TA,) said of God, (S, Msb,) He made him alive, to live, or be a living being; quickened, endued with life, vivified, [ revivified, revived, or resuscitated, ] him. (S, * Msb, * K.)

Hence, in the Kur [lxxv. last verse], A^alayosa *`lika biqaAdirK A^ano yuHoyiYa AlmawotaY , (S, TA,) i. e. Is not That Doer of these things (Jel) [ able to quicken the dead? ]. ― -b2- See also 2, in two places. ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) He (God) endued him with the intellectual faculty: as in the saying, in the Kur [vi. 122], A^awamano kaAna may~itFA faA^aHoyayonaAhu (assumed tropical:) [ And is he who was intellectually dead and whom we have endued with the intellectual faculty...? ]. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b4- See also

(S, K. [See also

is a particle, used in three senses: (Mughnee:) it is a particle denoting the end of an extent; (Mughnee, K;) which is its predominant meaning; (Mughnee;) asserted by some to be always its meaning: (TA:) and denoting a cause, or motive: and syn. with A_il~aA as an exceptive; (Mughnee, K;) which last is the rarest, and is mentioned by few. ; or must be prefixed to the word signifying that part, or portion, as in the saying, [in the Kur xcvii. last verse,] salaAmN hiYa Hat~aY maTolaEi Alfajori [A night of peace, or of salutation, is it, until the time of the rising of the dawn ]. (Mughnee.) It is also followed by a mansoob aor., as in sirotu Hat~aY A^adoxulahaA [ I journeyed until I entered it, AdxlhA here virtually meaning daxalotuhaA ], A^ano being here understood after Ht~Y , and the An together with the verb being rendered in grammatical analysis by an inf. n. governed in the gen. case by Ht~Y [so that Ht~Y An AdxlhA means Ht~Y duxuwliY A_iy~aAhaA ]: this is one of the cases in which Ht~Y differs from A_ilaY ; for one may not say, sirotu A_ilaY A^adoxulahaA [with A^ano understood after AlY ]: and in the same sense it is u

82 of the Arabic text;) others reading yaquwla , which, as well as yaquwlu , here means qaAla . (Jel.) ― -b7- [Respecting the cases in which the mansoob aor. is used after HA~Y , and those in which the marfooa aor. is used, the following observations are made.] When Ht~Y precedes a future, the latter is mansoob, by reason of A^ano understood before it, as in the saying, sirotu A_ilY Alkuwfapi Hat~aY A^adoxulahaA [ I journeyed to El-Koofeh until I entered it: see above]: (S:) it is not mansoob unless the verb is a future: if it is future with respect to the time of speaking, it must be mansoob, as in Hat~aY yarojiEa A_ilayonaA muwsaY [cited above]: if the verb is future with respect to what precedes, only, it may be mansoob, as in Hat~aY yaquwla Alr~asuwlu [mentioned above]

; or it may be marfooa; but not unless [somehow] denoting a present time; (Mughnee;) and if present with respect to the time of speaking, it must be marfooa, as in the saying, sirotu A_ilaY Alkuwfapi Hat~aY A^adoxuluhaA [ I have journeyed to El-Koofeh so that now I am entering it ]; (S, Mughnee; *) but if not really present, it is not marfooa unless denoting a past event as though it were present, as in Hat~aY yaquwlu Alr~asuwlu [explained above]; nor may it be marfooa unless denoting an effect of what precedes it; so that you may not say, sirotu Hat~aY taToluEu Al$~amosu , nor maA sirotu Hat~aY A^adoxuluhaA unless the mA is regarded as prefixed to the entire affirmative phrase that follows it, nor halo sirota Hat~aY tadoxuluhaA ; nor may it be marfooa unless it denote a complement to what

; or the becoming unoccupied by a thing; like $at~aY from Al$~at~u : but Az disapproves of this, because, were it so, the pronunciation termed A_imaAlap would be allowable in its case, and it is not so: Ht~Y , he says, is a particle, not a noun, nor a verb. (S.) ― -b13- In the dial. of Hudheyl, Eat~aY is said for Hat~aY . (L.)

You say, maAta Hatofa A^anofihi , (A 'Obeyd, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and Hatofa fiyhi , but this is rare, and Hatofa A^anofayohi , (K,) which may mean manoxirayohi , or it may mean A^anofh wafamh , the Anf being made predominant, (TA,) He died upon his bed; (A 'Obeyd, Mgh, Msb, K;) [ a natural death; ] respiring until he yielded his last breath; (Msb;) not from slaughter, nor beating, (A 'Obeyd, S, Msb, K,) nor drowning, nor burning, (A 'Obeyd, Sgh, Msb, K,) nor by a wild beast, &c.: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) the nose is particularized as meaning that the spirit passes forth from it with the breath

52.) It is said of a human being: (S, Mgh:) and then of any animal when it dies without any accidental cause: (Mgh:) hence, of a fish that has died, and floats upon the water. (Msb, TA.)
